'''{{ill|Kōzaki Shrine & Komori Shrine & Arasaki Shrine|ja|神前神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōzaki Shrine & Komori Shrine & Arasaki Shrine|qq=}}''' (*Kōzaki Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. It Ranks 18th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Compiled by Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9-11.</ref>
This article also covers the '''{{ill|Komori Shrine|ja|許母利神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Komori Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神前神社 (伊勢市)}}''' (*Komori Jinja*) and '''{{ill|Arasaki Shrine|ja|荒前神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arasaki Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神前神社 (伊勢市)|1=Kōzaki Shrine & Komori Shrine & Arasaki Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17228423}}''' (*Arasaki Jinja*), which are subordinate shrines (*massha*) enshrined alongside Kōzaki Shrine.
All three shrines are dedicated to the deities protecting the local coastline, despite being located inland from their original sites. The sound of waves can still be heard within the shrine grounds.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka Publishing (2008): p. 98.</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 73.</ref>
== Overview ==
This section describes information common to all three shrines.
The shrines are located on the summit of {{ill|Koidoguchiyama|ja|小井戸口山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koidoguchiyama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|Matsushita, Futami, Ise, Mie|ja|二見町松下|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsushita, Futami, Ise, Mie|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie|1=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}.<ref name="ic"/> The mountain is situated south of {{ill|Kōzaki Coast|ja|神崎海岸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōzaki Coast|1=Q11589649|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11589649}}.<ref name="gk"/> On this coast, the {{ill|Nieumi Shinto ritual|ja|贄海神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nieumi Shinto ritual|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was conducted, where sacred offerings ({{ill|Shinsen|en|Shinsen|qid=Q11591045|lt=shinsen|1=Shinsen}}) were gathered for {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|1=Amaterasu}}.<ref name="gk"/> The shrine grounds cover approximately 1,795 m².<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 11</ref>
== Kōzaki Shrine ==
The enshrined deity is Arasaki-hime-no-Mikoto (荒前比賣命).<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> She is the guardian deity of the coastal area of Matsushita in Futami.<ref name="ic"/> The same goddess is also enshrined at {{ill|Akasaki Shrine|ja|赤崎神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akasaki Shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Toba, Mie|en|Toba, Mie|qid=Q819629|lt=Toba, Mie|1=Toba, Mie}}, a subordinate shrine of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyōke Daijingū|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine), and at {{ill|Arasaki Shrine|ja|荒崎神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arasaki Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, with whom she is jointly enshrined. She is said to have been revered by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}.<ref name="tm2">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 80</ref> Arasaki-hime-no-Mikoto is considered the daughter of {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|建速須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} and the younger sister of {{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsuhime|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu-hime|qq=}}.<ref name="tm2"/>
== Komori Shrine ==
Komori Shrine is Ranked 5th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Inner Shrine of Ise.<ref name="uy2">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 13–14</ref> The main shrine has been discontinued, and the deity is jointly enshrined with Kōzaki Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 13</ref> Due to the name "Komori" (meaning "child protection"), prayers related to childbirth, safe delivery, and child growth have been offered here.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 78</ref>
The enshrined deity is Awashima-no-Kami Mitama (粟嶋神御魂).<ref name="ic"/> Like Arasaki-hime-no-Mikoto, Awashima-no-Kami is the guardian deity of the coastal area of Matsushita in Futami.<ref name="ic"/> This deity is identified with {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少名毘古那神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qid=Q3275687}} and is believed to have been enshrined to pacify the fierce nature of Arasaki-hime-no-Mikoto.<ref name="tm"/>
== Arasaki Shrine ==
Arasaki Shrine is Ranked 12th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Inner Shrine of Ise.<ref name="uy2"/> The main shrine has been discontinued.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 14</ref>
The enshrined deity is the same as that of Kōzaki Shrine, Arasaki-hime-no-Mikoto.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>
== History ==
According to the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, the shrines were established before the compilation of the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, that is, prior to {{ill|927|en|927|qid=Q30470|lt=927|1=927}}.<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22</ref> Tradition holds that when {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} toured Futami, she established {{ill|E Shrine|ja|江神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/E Shrine|qq=}}. After being welcomed by Arasaki-hime-no-Mikoto, Kōzaki Shrine was established in her honor.<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): pp. 94, 98</ref> 
Originally, the shrine grounds were located along the coast, but due to flooding and other factors, the shrines were relocated to the summit of Koidoguchiyama.<ref name="gk"/> Until the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}, transportation to Koidoguchiyama was inconvenient, leading to several relocations before settling at the current location.<ref name="tm2"/>
== Access ==
[[File:Kouzaki-jinja (Naiku) 02.jpg|right|160px|Stone steps leading to the shrine.]]
From the Hinodebashi East intersection on {{ill|Japan National Route 42|en|Japan National Route 42|qid=Q2003243|lt=National Route 42 (Japan)|1=Japan National Route 42}} in Matsushita, Futami, Ise City, head east, passing through gravel and dirt paths, and climb the stone steps to reach the shrine.<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): pp. 96–98</ref> There are approximately 280 stone steps.<ref name="gk"/> Among the 125 shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, this shrine is considered the second most challenging to access after {{ill|Kamo Shrine (Ise)|ja|鴨神社 (玉城町)|lt=Kamo Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo Shrine (Ise)|qq=}}.<ref name="tm2"/>
; Public Transportation
* Approximately an 18-minute walk (about 1.5 km) from {{ill|Matsushita Station|en|Matsushita Station|qid=Q93433|lt=Matsushita Station|1=Matsushita Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line|1=Sangū Line}} operated by {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central|1=Central Japan Railway Company}}.
* Approximately an 11-minute walk (about 900 m) from the ''Meotoiwa Higashiguchi'' bus stop served by {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu|1=Mie Kotsu}} buses.
; By Car
* Approximately 16 minutes (about 4.2 km) via {{ill|Ise Futami Toba Line|ja|伊勢二見鳥羽ライン|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Futami Toba Line|1=Ise Futami Toba Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11378935}} from {{ill|Futami Junction|ja|二見ジャンクション|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futami Junction|1=Futami junction|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10880410}}, through National Route 42. Note that there are no parking facilities nearby.
